task:
FIX TWO CODEX REVIEW FINDINGS ON PR #816 (F2d PR4b), review round 4. Update only the existing branch f2d/pr4b-probe-publish; its head must be a7d68133afe814ef05dfa9e78a683f74280df338 (full SHA from git rev-parse of origin/f2d/pr4b-probe-publish; if it differs, stop and report the SHA you found). Read CLAUDE.md and design sections 8.1, 8.3 and 8.6 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f2d-wide-archetype-and-product-attachment-design.md first. Both findings are confirmed by Claude; fix each with tests that FAIL on the current head (say which).

G1 (P1) scripts/operator/v3_production_deploy.py ~lines 608-704: is_f2d_release() is true for every candidate once 015 is installed, and validate_f2d_generation() refuses with finder_products_already_registered_on_parallel_v1 whenever any Finder product row exists on parallel_v1. After the go-live publication those rows exist for ever, so EVERY later production upgrade (preflight and promote) would refuse. Fix: the empty-Finder-products requirement of design 8.1 applies only to the FIRST F2d cutover, i.e. when the currently accepted release (accepted_release_schema_compatibility in the authority, the release being replaced) carries no F2d attestation group. For a later upgrade (the currently accepted release is itself an F2d release), do not require emptiness; instead require the exact parallel_v1 generation as now and that each Finder product row present is in an allowed state (READY with validation status VERIFIED, published or unpublished, or BUILDING/READY-unpublished during a rollout -- never FAILED), and record the observed product states in the receipt. Name the exact rule you implement and each refusal reason. Tests: first cutover with products present refuses (unchanged); later upgrade with both products READY+published passes; later upgrade with a FAILED product refuses; the rule keys off the currently accepted release, not off an optional dispatch value.

G2 (P1) unauthenticated wheels on the F2d path. Today every F2d action installs `psycopg[binary]==3.3.4` from a staged wheelhouse (.v3-probe-wheelhouse / .v3-search-wheelhouse / .v3-archetype-wheelhouse) that the workflows fill with `pip download` by version only; deploy/v3-production/f2d-operator-code.txt hashes only the requirement string, so substituted wheel bytes pass every identity check and are then imported with production write authority. Design 8.3 says the manifest pins "the exact psycopg requirement and wheel". Fix for the F2d path only: add a committed hash-locked requirements file (e.g. deploy/v3-production/f2d-wheels.txt) listing psycopg==3.3.4, psycopg-binary==3.3.4 and every transitive dependency pip resolves for CPython 3.14 on manylinux x86_64 (the API image's platform -- confirm from the Dockerfile/base image), each with --hash=sha256:... for the exact wheel files (compute them with `pip download --only-binary=:all: --platform ... --python-version 3.14 --implementation cp` and `pip hash`; record how in a comment). List that file in deploy/v3-production/f2d-operator-code.txt (keep sorted; update EXPECTED_ACTIVE_ENTRIES). In every F2d staging step of .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml and the publish-finder-products steps of .github/workflows/v3-production-application-deploy.yml, download with `pip download --require-hashes -r deploy/v3-production/f2d-wheels.txt ...` into the wheelhouse; in every F2d action's in-container install (v3-archetype-calibration-complete.sh, v3-finder-capacity-gate.sh, v3-system-search-f1.sh, v3-system-archetype.sh, v3-archetype-plan-probe.sh, v3-publish-derived-products.sh) install with `--no-index --find-links <wheelhouse> --require-hashes -r /work/deploy/v3-production/f2d-wheels.txt` instead of the bare requirement. The capacity-measurement workflow (.github/workflows/v3-finder-capacity-measurement.yml) installs into a disposable CI runner, not production: switch it to the same hash-locked file too if simple, otherwise leave it and say so. Do NOT change the non-F2d ratings-v4 / spatial actions or their workflows (separate follow-up). Tests: every F2d action's install line uses --require-hashes with the committed file; every F2d staging download uses --require-hashes; the hash file is in the operator-code manifest; a test parses f2d-wheels.txt and asserts every requirement line is exact-pinned with at least one sha256 hash.

ALLOWED FILES: scripts/operator/v3_production_deploy.py; tests/test_v3_release_gate_f2d.py; deploy/v3-production/f2d-wheels.txt (new); deploy/v3-production/f2d-operator-code.txt; tests/test_f2d_operator_identity.py (EXPECTED_ACTIVE_ENTRIES only); the six F2d action scripts named above; .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml; .github/workflows/v3-production-application-deploy.yml; .github/workflows/v3-finder-capacity-measurement.yml; the existing tests that assert those install/download lines (tests/test_v3_*operator*.py, tests/test_v3_publish_derived_products_operator.py, tests/test_v3_archetype_plan_probe_operator.py, tests/test_v3_finder_capacity_gate_operator.py, tests/test_v3_finder_capacity_measurement_workflow.py, tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_complete.py, tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_probe_operator.py, tests/test_v3_system_archetype_operator.py, tests/test_v3_system_search_production_operator.py, tests/test_v3_production_application_deployment.py) -- extend, never weaken; tests/test_f2d_wheels.py (new) if you prefer; CHANGES.md (amend the PR4b entry). Nothing else.

VALIDATION TO RUN AND REPORT WITH EXACT COUNTS: bash -n on all six actions; ruff check scripts tests; python -m pytest on every test file you touched plus tests/test_v3_release_gate_f2d.py tests/test_f2d_operator_identity.py tests/test_python314_execution_surfaces.py -q -p no:warnings; `pip download --require-hashes -r deploy/v3-production/f2d-wheels.txt` for the target platform succeeds; both identity helpers' compute output (equal); validate_authority on deploy/v3-production/target-authority.json (expect []). Code only; no deploy, no production access. End with: files changed; tests with counts and which fail on the previous head; the G1 rule; the exact wheel files and platform you pinned; anything you could not do.
